newsitem.title: USA: U.S. condemns annulment of elections by Belgrade. [CORRECTED 19:43 GMT]
newsitem.headline: U.S. condemns annulment of elections by Belgrade. [CORRECTED 19:43 GMT]

text.p: The United States on Monday condemned the annulment of municipal election results by the authorities in Belgrade which had produced victories for a coalition opposed to Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic.

State Department spokesman Glyn Davies told a news conference the annulment was "totally unacceptable" and said: "Such a step undermines the election process and invalidates Serbia's claim to be a state evolving towards democracy."

Davies said that in recent meetings in Paris, Secretary of State Warren Christopher had told Yugoslav Foreign Minister Milan Milutinovic that "Serbia could not expect to rejoin the international community until it demonstrated commitment to developing into a modern, open and democratic society."
(Corrects spelling of foreign minister's surname and his country).

He said: "Because of Serbia's failure to observe democratic principles, the United States has not recognised Belgrade. This recent action confirms our position that Serbia is not committed to meeting western democratic standards..." Washington maintains an embassy in Belgrade but does not formally recognise the government there.

In answer to a question, Davies said the United States response to Belgrade at this stage was to "talk about what is going on there and basically shine a spotlight on what we believe the ruling party has been up to" but he said this "would not preclude other actions might be taken."

After polling eight days ago, Milosevic's Socialists initially conceded they had lost councils in industrial towns across Serbia including the capital Belgrade. But state-controlled electoral commissions, citing unspecified irregularites, later annulled the results in almost all the districts won by the opposition Zajedno coalition.
